newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Fraser & Neaves falls, earnings revised.
newsitem.headline: Fraser & Neaves falls, earnings revised.

text.p: Soft drink company Fraser & Neave Ltd (F&N) fell to a new year low of Singapore $10 per share on Monday after announcing an 18 percent drop in half year profit, analysts and dealers said.
F&N, which is also in property development and dairy operations, was trading around S$10.30, down S$0.20 on 839,000 shares at 0420 GMT.

On Friday the group, which produces some of the world's most popular carbonated drinks including Coca Cola, Diet Coke and Sprite, reported net profit dropped to S$83.54 million in the half year ending march 31.
The company also said it expected weaker full-year results.
Contributions from its soft drink were dampened by the loss of three months production due to a strike in Sri Lanka, price cuts in Pakistan and heavy investment costs in Vietnam.
The bulk of the profits came from brewery operations which saw a pre-tax profit of S$91 million, underpinned by Singapore, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea and Malaysia.
Vietnam saw lower profits due to higher depreciation costs and currency devaluation. Cambodia suffered from start-up losses.
F&N's property company, Centrepoint Properties Ltd saw a 34 percent profit drop to S$41 million due to lower development profits.
According to the Edinburgh Publishing's Estimate Directory, the group's full year net profit was expected to fall 20 percent to around S$172 million.
After the half-year results, several research houses said they were revising their earnings forecasts down for F&N,

"For the full year, we are lowering our profit forecast from S$172 million to S$167 million due to lower contribution from its dairy operations high start up costs," said Paul Heng, an investment analyst at Fraser-AMMB Research.
"There is no way they are going to meet the consensus of S$172 million. Second half cannot be that much better," said an analyst with a local brokerage house.
The group had already booked most of its profits from property developments, analysts said.
The brewery operations in the second half were expected to face continued high start-up costs in China, Burma and Cambodia.
However, most analysts said they see good fundamental support for F&N at S$10.00.

"F&N share price has fallen about 25 percent since early this year. At S$10.50, the shares are trading at 18 times prospective price earning for 1997, which is reasonably attractive," said Heng of Fraser, which was recommneding an accumulate for the stocks.
